questions.q: A reporter has a strong line of action, a scientist tracking a rare bird for a season, but no dramatic resolution. What would Hart suggest?
choices: Give up on narrative and write an inverted pyramid
Invent a resolution
Turn it into a five-act tragedy
Write an explanatory narrative: let the line of action carry the reader through digressions
questions.explain: Hart's explanatory narrative uses a narrative line to carry an explanation and doesn't need a resolution.

choices: They are the same thing
Narrative is fiction; story is fact
A story has a full arc with complication and resolution; narrative is any writing that moves through time with scenes and characters
Story is what happened; narrative is the emotional insight
questions.explain: Every story is a narrative, but not every narrative is a story.

questions.q: In Hart's arc, what is the 'point of insight'?
choices: The paragraph that explains why the story matters now
The moment the protagonist sees the situation in a new way, allowing the complication to be resolved
The reporter's first-person reflection
The opening scene
questions.explain: Hart, following Franklin, stresses that change in true stories is often a change of understanding.

choices: A list, in order, of the developments that turn a story in a new direction, made before writing
A list of every quotation in the notebook
A list of the six dimensions of a trend story
The legal checklist for publication
questions.explain: It does for a long narrative what Franklin's short outline does for a shorter one.

questions.q: Which thinker's definition of story does Hart build on directly?
choices: Vivian Gornick's
Tom Wolfe's
Blake Snyder's
Jon Franklin's
questions.explain: Hart keeps Franklin's protagonist–complication–resolution definition and expands it.

questions.q: A draft summarizes a dramatic hospital night in two sentences, then spends a full scene on a routine staff meeting. What's the problem in Hart's terms?
choices: The point of view keeps shifting
It needs a nut graf
Scene and summary are used the wrong way round: save full scenes for the moments that matter most
There are too many plot points
questions.explain: Scenes slow time for important moments; summary moves quickly through the rest.

questions.q: Which critique applies to Hart's approach?
choices: It forbids scenes in nonfiction
Its techniques can turn every subject into a human-interest story with a protagonist and an epiphany
It ignores reporting entirely
It rejects the narrative arc
questions.explain: Critics argue narrative techniques can push stories about systems toward individual arcs.

ideas: Every story is a narrative, but not every narrative is a story: some forms carry a reader without a full arc.
A true story often turns on a point of insight, when the protagonist finally sees the situation in a new way.
When a story has no resolution, let a line of action carry the reader through an explanation instead.
Before drafting, list the plot points: each development that turns the story in a new direction.
